verdict.summary: ServiceNow has no central developer app and no central OAuth approval. Each customer's admin registers your OAuth client in the Application Registry on their own instance, so you set it up once per instance and no review is involved. Review only happens if you choose to list a scoped app on the ServiceNow Store, which requires Build Partner status and certification.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min per instance (plus 1-2 days of document prep if you go for a Store listing)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 min, once you have admin access to an instance
verdict.approval_wait: None for OAuth. A Store listing (optional) takes roughly 3-5 weeks of certification, according to ServiceNow's guidance.

gates.name: OAuth client on your own instance
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own ServiceNow account through Composio. You register an inbound OAuth client in the Application Registry (or the Machine Identity Console) on an instance where you are admin.
limits: Requires the admin role on the instance
Access tokens last 30 min and refresh tokens last 100 days by default (Refresh Token Lifespan field)
The authorize and token URLs are specific to each instance

gates.name: Customer instances (admin-registered client)
gates.unlocks: Users on a customer's instance can connect once that customer's admin registers your client in their instance's Application Registry and gives you the client ID, secret and instance subdomain.
limits: One registration per customer instance: there is no shared client across instances
No user or install cap was found for unreviewed clients
Token lifetimes are set per instance (defaults: 30 min access, 100 days refresh)
gates.time_to_reach: Same day per customer. It depends on how quickly the customer admin acts.

gates.name: Anyone (per-instance OAuth); optional ServiceNow Store listing
gates.unlocks: Any ServiceNow customer can use your integration by registering the OAuth client themselves. ServiceNow does not review OAuth clients. A Store listing, distributed as a certified scoped app, is optional and the only path that goes through review.
limits: Store listing requires Build Partner status
Store apps must be scoped (not global)
Store apps can need recertification for new ServiceNow releases and for code changes
Customers must accept the Store terms before installing any Store app
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for per-instance OAuth. A Store listing takes about 3-5 weeks of certification (ServiceNow guidance) and can take longer.

steps.title: Get admin access to a ServiceNow instance
steps.detail: Sign in to the ServiceNow Developer site, or use an existing instance where you have the admin role. The OAuth client has to be registered by an admin on that instance.
gotchas: The developer site needs JavaScript and a supported browser.

steps.title: Collect the instance subdomain
steps.detail: Record the instance subdomain (the part before .service-now.com). Composio builds the authorize and token URLs from it: https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and /oauth_token.do.

steps.title: Create a ServiceNow OAuth2 auth config in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the servicenow toolkit using OAUTH2 with your own credentials, because Composio offers no managed app for ServiceNow. Copy the callback URL Composio shows; you need it in the next step.
gotchas: Composio has no managed OAuth for ServiceNow, so you must bring your own client.

steps.title: Register the OAuth client in the Application Registry
steps.detail: On the instance, go to System OAuth > Application Registry, click New, and choose 'Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients'. On Zurich and later, use the Machine Identity Console > Inbound Integrations instead and pick the authorization code grant there.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The menu path depends on the release. Older releases use the Application Registry; newer ones use the Machine Identity Console.
Do not mark the client as Public Client: Composio holds the secret, so it is a confidential client.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URL to the Composio callback
steps.detail: In the registry record's Redirect URL field, paste the exact Composio callback URL. For authorization-code flows the redirect points at the connecting app, and it must match exactly what Composio sends.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A mismatch causes an 'Invalid Redirect_URI' error.

steps.title: Copy credentials and scope into Composio
steps.detail: Save the registry record, then copy its Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio auth config along with the instance subdomain. Keep the default scope useraccount unless you have created narrower auth scopes.
gotchas: useraccount grants everything the connecting user's roles allow.

steps.title: Optionally restrict access with REST API Auth Scopes
steps.detail: If you want least-privilege access, create sys_auth_scope records and attach them to REST APIs through the REST API Auth Scope form (plugin com.glide.rest.auth.scope, Tokyo and later). Then assign that scope to the OAuth client. For example, a read-only scope allows only GET on the Table API.
gotchas: Table-level control may sit in API Access Policies rather than auth scopes, depending on the release.
Clients without the scope get a 403 on any API that requires it.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, log in to the instance, approve access, and make a test API call. Then check that the token refreshes: access tokens expire after 30 min and refresh tokens after 100 days by default.
gotchas: Setups copied from older guides have returned server_error or access_denied on Zurich. Follow the docs for the instance's release.

steps.title: Prepare onboarding instructions for customer admins
steps.detail: Draft a short guide for each customer's admin. It should tell them to register the client in their own Application Registry (or Machine Identity Console) with the Composio Redirect URL, then send you the client ID, secret and instance subdomain. Each customer instance needs its own registration.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Ask each customer which release they run, because the menu paths differ.

steps.title: Customer admin registers the client
steps.detail: Each customer's admin completes the registration on their instance, and you add their credentials and subdomain to a Composio auth config. ServiceNow runs no central review for this.

steps.title: (Optional Store listing) Become a Build Partner and build a scoped app
steps.detail: Do this only if you want a ServiceNow Store listing. You need Build Partner status (the general Partner Program is not enough), and the app must be scoped rather than global.
gotchas: Global-scope apps cannot be published to the Store.

steps.title: (Optional) Run Validate Application and prepare certification documents
steps.detail: On the app record in the vendor instance, run the Self-Test tool with Validate Application at least once on the exact version you will submit. Draft the design document, the test plan with results, the customer installation guide, and the listing materials.
gotchas: The full checklist is in the Store Publisher Portal knowledge base, which needs a separate login.

steps.title: (Optional) Publish to the Store and request certification
steps.detail: From the app record, select Publish to ServiceNow Store, then request certification in the Store Publisher Portal (tpp.servicenow.com).

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for certification
steps.detail: The certification team reviews security, performance, stability, user experience, the install process, architecture and the listing. ServiceNow's guidance says this typically takes 3-5 weeks, longer if fixes are needed.
gotchas: Recertification can be needed for new ServiceNow releases and for code changes.

requirements.item: Admin role on the ServiceNow instance
requirements.detail: Registering the inbound OAuth client requires the admin role.
The authorize and token URLs are specific to each instance, so you need the subdomain before the flow can start.

requirements.item: Redirect URL that exactly matches the Composio callback
requirements.detail: The value saved in the registry must match the redirect URI Composio sends.
Each customer's admin registers the client in their own instance's Application Registry.
Required to list an app on the ServiceNow Store.
Global-scope apps cannot be published to the Store.

requirements.item: Self-Test (Validate Application) run on the submitted version (Store only)
requirements.detail: Must be run at least once on the exact version you submit.

requirements.item: Design document, test plan with results, installation guide, listing materials (Store only)
requirements.detail: Needed for the App Review and Listing Review certification tracks.

scopes.effect: Available by default and used as Composio's default scope. No review is needed, but it grants everything the user's profile and roles permit.

scopes.scope: Custom auth scopes (sys_auth_scope) via REST API Auth Scope
scopes.effect: Optional, admin-defined scopes that limit a client to specific REST APIs (for example, GET-only on the Table API). Clients without the scope get a 403. No provider review is involved; behavior varies by release.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI Composio sends does not match the Redirect URL saved in the registry record.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the registry record's Redirect URL field.

blockers.symptom: server_error or access_denied on Zurich after following an older guide
blockers.cause: Differences between releases. Zurich moves inbound OAuth setup into the Machine Identity Console.
blockers.fix: Configure the client through Machine Identity Console > Inbound Integrations and follow the docs for the instance's release.

blockers.cause: The system property glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled defaults to false.
blockers.fix: Set the property to true if you use client credentials. Composio's standard flow uses the authorization code grant instead.

blockers.symptom: Cannot list the app on the ServiceNow Store
blockers.cause: You are not a Build Partner, or the app is global-scoped.
blockers.fix: Get Build Partner status and package the integration as a scoped app.

blockers.symptom: Not allowed to market the app as ServiceNow-certified
blockers.cause: The certified label requires distribution exclusively through the ServiceNow Store.
blockers.fix: Distribute only through the Store, or do not claim certification.

blockers.symptom: Customer cannot install your Store app
blockers.cause: The customer has not accepted the Store terms and conditions.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer to accept the Store terms on their instance.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for ServiceNow, so you must bring your own client from the start. Each customer runs its own instance, which means you need a client ID, secret and instance subdomain per customer, registered by that customer's admin in their Application Registry. The authorize and token URLs follow https://{subdomain}.service-now.com/oauth_auth.do and oauth_token.do.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit record shows no managed OAuth for ServiceNow; the only OAuth2 entry is generic, with useraccount as its default scope and instance-specific authorize and token URLs.
evidence.quote: managed_oauth_available: false; default_scopes: ["useraccount"]

evidence.claim: A client assigned a read-only auth scope gets only GET access on the Table API; other methods return 403.
evidence.quote: any access token issued for this OAuth client will only allow GET requests

evidence.claim: Auth scopes are created as sys_auth_scope records and attached to a REST API through the REST API Auth Scope form; clients without the scope are blocked.
evidence.quote: its absence will block clients that do not have it from leveraging the resource in question

open_questions: No official source confirms whether unreviewed OAuth clients face any user or install cap. None is expected, because the clients are per-instance.
The exact menu path (Application Registry or Machine Identity Console) and field labels depend on the release. Confirm them on each customer's release.
The authorization-code procedure on the official docs page could not be read. Refresh-token details come from community posts.
No ServiceNow concept of sensitive or restricted scopes, and no scope review, was found. Access appears to depend on the connecting user's roles.
The 3-5 week Store certification figure is from 2023 guidance and may be out of date. The 1-7 day figure is unofficial.
Build Partner costs and tier requirements were not verified on a ServiceNow-owned page.
No live authorize-endpoint response was observed, because the probe was blocked.
